claim: Drosophila male courtship is controlled by the male-specific products of the fruitless (fruM) gene and its expressing neuronal circuitry.
source: Drosophila male courtship is controlled by the male-specific products of the fruitless (fruM) gene and its expressing neuronal circuitry.
evidence: This is a foundational statement supported by established scientific knowledge and citations in the field.

claim: fruM is considered a master gene that controls all aspects of male courtship.
source: fruM is considered a master gene that controls all aspects of male courtship.
evidence: This represents the conventional view in the field, supported by prior research and citations.

claim: fruM is required during a critical developmental period for innate courtship toward females.
source: By temporally and spatially manipulating fruM expression, we found that fruM is required during a critical developmental period for innate courtship toward females
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from temporal manipulation experiments shown in Figure 1.

claim: fruM function during adulthood is involved in inhibiting male–male courtship.
source: we found that fruM is required during a critical developmental period for innate courtship toward females, while its function during adulthood is involved in inhibiting male–male courtship.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from adult-specific manipulation experiments shown in Figure 2.

claim: Males can be generated that are innately heterosexual, homosexual, bisexual, or without innate courtship but could acquire such behavior in an experience-dependent manner by altering or eliminating fruM expression.
source: By altering or eliminating fruM expression, we generated males that are innately heterosexual, homosexual, bisexual, or without innate courtship but could acquire such behavior in an experience-dependent manner.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from various fruM manipulation experiments shown in Figure 3.

claim: fruM is not absolutely necessary for courtship but is critical during development to build a sex circuitry with reduced flexibility and enhanced efficiency.
source: These findings show that fruM is not absolutely necessary for courtship but is critical during development to build a sex circuitry with reduced flexibility and enhanced efficiency
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data showing experience-dependent courtship acquisition in fruM null males.

claim: fruM tunes functional flexibility of a sex circuitry instead of switching on its function as conventionally viewed.
source: provide a new view about how fruM tunes functional flexibility of a sex circuitry instead of switching on its function as conventionally viewed.
evidence: This is the main interpretive conclusion of the study, based on the experimental data showing different courtship modes with different fruM expression patterns.

claim: The fru gene and its expressing neurons control most aspects of innate male courtship behavior.
source: It has been well established that the fruitless (fru) gene and its expressing neurons control most aspects of such innate behavior (Ito et al., 1996; Manoli et al., 2005; Ryner et al., 1996; Stockinger et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: The male-specific products of the P1 promoter of the fru gene (fruM) are expressed in ~2000 neurons.
source: The male-specific products of the P1 promoter of the fru gene (fruM) are expressed in ~2000 neurons, which are inter-connected to form a sex circuitry from sensory neurons to motor neurons (Cachero et al., 2010; Lee et al., 2000; Manoli et al., 2005; Stockinger et al., 2005; Usui-Aoki et al., 2000; Yu et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: fruM-expressing neurons are inter-connected to form a sex circuitry from sensory neurons to motor neurons.
source: The male-specific products of the P1 promoter of the fru gene (fruM) are expressed in ~2000 neurons, which are inter-connected to form a sex circuitry from sensory neurons to motor neurons (Cachero et al., 2010; Lee et al., 2000; Manoli et al., 2005; Stockinger et al., 2005; Usui-Aoki et al., 2000; Yu et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: fruM function is necessary for the innate courtship behavior.
source: fruM function is necessary for the innate courtship behavior and sufficient for at least some aspects of courtship (Baker et al., 2001; Demir and Dickson, 2005; Manoli et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: fruM function is sufficient for at least some aspects of courtship.
source: fruM function is necessary for the innate courtship behavior and sufficient for at least some aspects of courtship (Baker et al., 2001; Demir and Dickson, 2005; Manoli et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Males without fruM function, although did not court if raised in isolation, were able to acquire at least some courtship behaviors if raised in groups.
source: Although fruM serves as a master gene controlling Drosophila male courtship, we recently found that males without fruM function, although did not court if raised in isolation, were able to acquire at least some courtship behaviors if raised in groups (Pan and Baker, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research by the authors.

claim: fruM-independent but experience-dependent courtship acquisition requires the doublesex (dsx) gene.
source: Such fruM-independent but experience-dependent courtship acquisition requires another gene in the sex determination pathway, the doublesex (dsx) gene (Pan and Baker, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research by the authors.

claim: dsx encodes male- and female-specific DSX proteins (DSXM and DSXF, respectively).
source: dsx encodes male- and female-specific DSX proteins (DSXM and DSXF, respectively) (Burtis and Baker, 1989)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: DSXM is expressed in ~700 neurons in the central nervous system (CNS).
source: DSXM is expressed in ~700 neurons in the central nervous system (CNS), the majority of which also express fruM (Rideout et al., 2010; Robinett et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The majority of DSXM-expressing neurons also express fruM.
source: DSXM is expressed in ~700 neurons in the central nervous system (CNS), the majority of which also express fruM (Rideout et al., 2010; Robinett et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The fruM and dsxM co-expressing neurons are required for courtship in the absence of fruM function.
source: It has been found that the fruM and dsxM co-expressing neurons are required for courtship in the absence of fruM function (Pan and Baker, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research by the authors.

claim: fruM-expressing neurons control the expression of courtship behaviors even in the absence of FRUM function.
source: Thus fruM-expressing neurons, especially those co-expressing dsxM, control the expression of courtship behaviors even in the absence of FRUM function.
evidence: This is an inference based on the cited finding about fruM and dsxM co-expressing neurons.

claim: The gross neuroanatomical features of the fruM-expressing circuitry are largely unaffected by the loss of fruM.
source: Indeed, although the gross neuroanatomical features of the fruM-expressing circuitry are largely unaffected by the loss of fruM (Manoli et al., 2005; Stockinger et al., 2005), detailed analysis revealed morphological changes of many fruM-expressing neurons (Cachero et al., 2010; Kimura et al., 2005; Kimura et al., 2008; Mellert et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Detailed analysis revealed morphological changes of many fruM-expressing neurons upon loss of fruM.
source: Indeed, although the gross neuroanatomical features of the fruM-expressing circuitry are largely unaffected by the loss of fruM (Manoli et al., 2005; Stockinger et al., 2005), detailed analysis revealed morphological changes of many fruM-expressing neurons (Cachero et al., 2010; Kimura et al., 2005; Kimura et al., 2008; Mellert et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: FRUM specifies neuronal development by recruiting chromatin factors and changing chromatin states.
source: Recent studies further reveal that FRUM specifies neuronal development by recruiting chromatin factors and changing chromatin states, and also by turning on and off the activity of the transcription repressor complex (Ito et al., 2012; Ito et al., 2016; Sato et al., 2019a; Sato et al., 2019b; Sato and Yamamoto, 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to recent research.

claim: FRUM specifies neuronal development by turning on and off the activity of the transcription repressor complex.
source: Recent studies further reveal that FRUM specifies neuronal development by recruiting chromatin factors and changing chromatin states, and also by turning on and off the activity of the transcription repressor complex (Ito et al., 2012; Ito et al., 2016; Sato et al., 2019a; Sato et al., 2019b; Sato and Yamamoto, 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to recent research.

claim: FRUM functions as a transcription factor to specify development and/or physiological roles of certain fruM-expressing neurons.
source: That FRUM functions as a transcription factor to specify development and/or physiological roles of certain fruM-expressing neurons, and perhaps the interconnection of different fruM-expressing neurons to form a sex circuitry raises important questions regarding when fruM functions and how it contributes to the sex circuitry
evidence: This is based on the cited research about FRUM's molecular mechanisms.

claim: Knocking down fruM in all the fruGAL4-labeled neurons eliminated male courtship toward females (courtship index nearly 0).
source: Knocking down fruM in all the fruGAL4-labeled neurons eliminated male courtship toward females (courtship index [CI], which is the percentage of observational time that males displayed courtship, is nearly 0) (Figure 1A)
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Males with fruM knocked down at stage 5 for 2 days, matching the pupation phase, rarely courted (CI < 10%).
source: We found that males with fruM knocked down at stage 5 for 2 days, matching the pupation phase, rarely courted (CI < 10%), and none successfully mated
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C and 1D.

claim: Males with fruM knocked down at stage 5 for 2 days did not successfully mate.
source: We found that males with fruM knocked down at stage 5 for 2 days, matching the pupation phase, rarely courted (CI < 10%), and none successfully mated
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Males with fruM knocked down near stage 5 (stages 4 and 6) showed a partial courtship or mating deficit.
source: while males with fruM knocked down near this period (stages 4 and 6) showed a partial courtship or mating deficit
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C and 1D.

claim: Males with fruM knocked down at earlier or later stages than stage 5 showed strong courtship toward females and successful mating.
source: and males with fruM knocked down at earlier or later stages showed strong courtship toward females and successful mating (Figure 1C,D).
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C and 1D.

claim: Two day heat shock at 30°C effectively knocks down fruM expression during development.
source: To test whether 2 day heat shock at 30°C is sufficient to knockdown fruM expression, we dissected brains of tub-GAL80ts/UAS-fruMi; fruGAL4/fruV5 males immediately after 2 day heat shock at stage 5 or 7 and found that anti-V5 and anti-FruM signals were both dramatically decreased
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E-H.

claim: Anti-V5 and anti-FruM signals were dramatically decreased after 2 day heat shock at stage 5 or 7.
source: we dissected brains of tub-GAL80ts/UAS-fruMi; fruGAL4/fruV5 males immediately after 2 day heat shock at stage 5 or 7 and found that anti-V5 and anti-FruM signals were both dramatically decreased, such that only a small fraction of neurons could be weakly labeled
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E-H.

claim: Males that have been heat shocked at earlier stages (from stages 1 to 5) still have strong FruM expression in adulthood.
source: Thus, we dissected brains of adult tub-GAL80ts/UAS-fruMi; fruGAL4/fruV5 males that have been heat shocked for 2 days at different developmental stages (from stages 1 to 9) and found that males that have been heat shocked at earlier stages (from stages 1 to 5) still have strong FruM expression (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A–F), suggesting effective restore of FruM expression after transferring at 18°C.
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3A-F.

claim: Males that have been heat shocked at later stages (stages 6–9) have obviously reduced FruM expression in adulthood.
source: However, males that have been heat shocked at later stages (stages 6–9) have obviously reduced FruM expression (Figure 1—figure supplement 3G–J), suggesting a partial restore of FruM expression, probably due to prolonged fruM microRNA effect.
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3G-J.

claim: All males heat shocked at stage 5 for 2 days showed defect of midline crossing in fruM-positive GRNs innervating VNC.
source: Interestingly, we found that all males heat shocked at stage 5 for 2 days showed defect of midline crossing in these GRNs
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4C and 4D.

claim: 60% of males heat shocked at stage 6 for 2 days showed defect of midline crossing in fruM-positive GRNs innervating VNC.
source: and 60% of males heat shocked at stage 6 for 2 days showed defect of midline crossing
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4C and 4D.

claim: All males heat shocked after stage 6 showed regular midline crossing in fruM-positive GRNs innervating VNC.
source: while all males heat shocked after stage 6 showed regular midline crossing (Figure 1—figure supplement 4C,D).
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4C and 4D.

claim: Males heat shocked for 4 days during adulthood have regular midline crossing in fruM-positive GRNs innervating VNC.
source: Males heat shocked for 4 days during adulthood also have regular midline crossing (Figure 1—figure supplement 4C,D).
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4C and 4D.

claim: There is a critical developmental period during pupation where FruM functions to ensure regular development of GRNs and enable innate male courtship toward females.
source: These results clearly showed a critical developmental period during pupation where FruM functions to ensure regular development of GRNs and enable innate male courtship toward females.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data on temporal knockdown and GRN morphology.

claim: Overexpression of traF in all fruGAL4 labeled neurons during adulthood for 4 days did not affect male–female courtship.
source: We found that overexpression of traF in all fruGAL4 labeled neurons during adulthood for 4 days did not affect male–female courtship (Figure 2A)
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Overexpression of traF in all fruGAL4 labeled neurons during adulthood for 4 days slightly increased male–male courtship.
source: We found that overexpression of traF in all fruGAL4 labeled neurons during adulthood for 4 days did not affect male–female courtship (Figure 2A), but slightly increased male–male (Figure 2B) and male chaining behaviors (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Overexpression of traF in all fruGAL4 labeled neurons during adulthood for 4 days slightly increased male chaining behaviors.
source: We found that overexpression of traF in all fruGAL4 labeled neurons during adulthood for 4 days did not affect male–female courtship (Figure 2A), but slightly increased male–male (Figure 2B) and male chaining behaviors (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Knocking down fruM in all fruGAL4-labeled neurons during adulthood for 4 days did not affect male–female courtship.
source: Furthermore, knocking down fruM in all fruGAL4-labeled neurons during adulthood for 4 days did not affect male–female (Figure 2A) or male–male courtship (Figure 2B)
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Knocking down fruM in all fruGAL4-labeled neurons during adulthood for 4 days did not affect male–male courtship.
source: Furthermore, knocking down fruM in all fruGAL4-labeled neurons during adulthood for 4 days did not affect male–female (Figure 2A) or male–male courtship (Figure 2B)
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Knocking down fruM in all fruGAL4-labeled neurons during adulthood for 4 days significantly increased male chaining behaviors.
source: Furthermore, knocking down fruM in all fruGAL4-labeled neurons during adulthood for 4 days did not affect male–female (Figure 2A) or male–male courtship (Figure 2B), but significantly increased male chaining behaviors (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: FruM expression was almost eliminated after 4 days heat shock during adulthood.
source: We also checked FruM expression in males that have been heat shocked for 4 days during adulthood using anti-V5 and anti-FruM antibodies, and found that FruM expression was almost eliminated, while control males have regular FruM expression (Figure 2D,E).
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D and 2E.

claim: fruM function during adulthood is dispensable for female-directed courtship.
source: These results indicate that although fruM function during adulthood is dispensable for female-directed courtship, it is involved in inhibiting male–male courtship behaviors.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data on adult-specific manipulation.

claim: fruM function during adulthood is involved in inhibiting male–male courtship behaviors.
source: These results indicate that although fruM function during adulthood is dispensable for female-directed courtship, it is involved in inhibiting male–male courtship behaviors.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data on adult-specific manipulation.

claim: FruM has distinct functions during development and adulthood for male courtship behaviors.
source: Thus, FruM has distinct functions during development and adulthood for male courtship behaviors.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the combined experimental data on temporal manipulation.

claim: Wild-type males performed intensive courtship behavior toward virgin females (CI > 80%).
source: We found that wild-type males performed intensive courtship behavior toward virgin females (CI > 80%) and rarely courted males (CI ~0) (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Wild-type males rarely courted males (CI ~0).
source: We found that wild-type males performed intensive courtship behavior toward virgin females (CI > 80%) and rarely courted males (CI ~0) (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Wild-type control males did not show any chaining behavior after grouping from 3 hr to 3 days (ChI = 0).
source: Furthermore, these control males did not show any chaining behavior after grouping from 3 hr to 3 days (ChI = 0) (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: fruM null mutant males rarely courted either females or males.
source: In striking contrast, fruM null mutant males rarely courted either females or males (Figure 3C, Figure 3—figure supplement 2A, C, and E)
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C and supplementary figures.

claim: fruM null mutant males developed intensive chaining behavior after grouping for 1–3 days.
source: however, these males developed intensive chaining behavior after grouping for 1–3 days (Figure 3D, Figure 3—figure supplement 2B, D, and F).
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D and supplementary figures.

claim: The fruM microRNA (UAS-fruMi at attp40) reduced fruM mRNA level to ~40% of that in control males.
source: We found that the fruM mRNA level was reduced to ~40% of that in control males (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: Males with fruM knocked down in all fruM neurons rarely courted females (CI ~5%).
source: Interestingly, while males with fruM knocked down in all fruM neurons rarely courted females (CI ~5%, Figure 3G)
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3G.

claim: Males with fruM knocked down in all fruM neurons displayed a high level of male–male courtship behavior (CI > 50%).
source: while males with fruM knocked down in all fruM neurons rarely courted females (CI ~5%, Figure 3G), they displayed a high level of male–male courtship behavior (CI > 50%, Figure 3G)
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3G.

claim: Males with fruM knocked down in all fruM neurons showed constantly high level of male chaining.
source: they displayed a high level of male–male courtship behavior (CI > 50%, Figure 3G) and constantly high level of male chaining (Figure 3H)
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3H.

claim: Males with fruM knocked down specifically in brain had a reduced level of courtship toward females (CI = 56.61 ± 5.86%).
source: We found that males with fruM knocked down specifically in brain had a reduced level of courtship toward females (CI = 56.61 ± 5.86%), but their sexual orientation was not changed as they courted males in a much lower level (CI = 15.94 ± 3.26%, Figure 3J).
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3J.

claim: Males with fruM knocked down specifically in brain courted males in a much lower level (CI = 15.94 ± 3.26%) than females.
source: We found that males with fruM knocked down specifically in brain had a reduced level of courtship toward females (CI = 56.61 ± 5.86%), but their sexual orientation was not changed as they courted males in a much lower level (CI = 15.94 ± 3.26%, Figure 3J).
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3J.

claim: Males with fruM knocked down in brain showed low male chaining behavior initially (ChI [3 hr] = 9.35 ± 5.40%) but increasing levels of chaining behavior over 1–3 days (ChI[3d] = 68.82 ± 5.53%).
source: Furthermore, males with fruM knocked down in brain showed low male chaining behavior initially but increasing levels of chaining behavior over 1–3 days (ChI [3 hr] = 9.35 ± 5.40%, ChI[3d] = 68.82 ± 5.53%, Figure 3K).
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3K.

claim: Knocking down fruM only in P1 neurons failed to decrease male–female courtship or induce male chaining behavior.
source: Knocking down fruM only in a subset of male-specific P1 neurons driven by P1-splitGAL4 in the brain that are important for courtship initiation (Clowney et al., 2015; Kallman et al., 2015; Kimura et al., 2008; Pan et al., 2012; Wu et al., 2019) failed to decrease male–female courtship or induce male chaining behavior (Figure 3—figure supplement 4A,B).
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4A and 4B.

claim: fruM function in brain promotes male–female courtship and inhibits acquisition or progression of the experience-dependent chaining behavior.
source: These results indicate that fruM function in brain promotes male–female courtship and inhibits acquisition or progression of the experience-dependent chaining behavior (Figure 3L).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data on brain-specific knockdown.

claim: Males with fruM knocked down outside brain showed equally intensive male–female and male–male courtship (CI [male–female] = 85.62 ± 1.42%, CI [male–male] = 82.89 ± 2.76%).
source: In contrast, males with fruM knocked down outside brain showed equally intensive male–female and male–male courtship (CI [male–female] = 85.62 ± 1.42%, CI [male–male] = 82.89 ± 2.76%, Figure 3M)
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3M.

claim: fruM in neurons outside brain has an inhibitory role for male–male courtship.
source: In contrast, males with fruM knocked down outside brain showed equally intensive male–female and male–male courtship (CI [male–female] = 85.62 ± 1.42%, CI [male–male] = 82.89 ± 2.76%, Figure 3M), indicating an inhibitory role of fruM in these neurons for male–male courtship (Figure 3O).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data on outside-brain knockdown.

claim: Males with fruM knocked down outside brain performed a high level of male chaining behavior initially (ChI [3 hr] = 92.90 ± 3.08%), but decreased levels of chaining behavior over 1–3 days (ChI [3d] = 20.01 ± 3.75%).
source: These males performed a high level of male chaining behavior initially (ChI [3 hr] = 92.90 ± 3.08%), but decreased levels of chaining behavior over 1–3 days (ChI [3d] = 20.01 ± 3.75%, Figure 3N)
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3N.

claim: Knocking down fruM in ppk23-expressing gustatory receptor neurons mildly enhanced male–male courtship but did not induce male chaining behavior.
source: Knocking down fruM in a subset of gustatory receptor neurons expressing ppk23 that respond to female-specific pheromones (Lu et al., 2012; Thistle et al., 2012; Toda et al., 2012) mildly enhanced male–male courtship but did not induce male chaining behavior (Figure 3—figure supplement 4C,D)
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4C and 4D.

claim: Different fruM expression levels and patterns determine courtship modes, indicative of functional flexibility of the fruM-expressing sex circuitry tuned by fruM function.
source: Taken together, the above results demonstrate distinct roles of fruM expression during a critical developmental period for the manifestation of courtship behaviors and adulthood for inhibiting male–male courtship (Figure 4A), and further reveal that different fruM expression levels and patterns determine courtship modes, indicative of functional flexibility of the fruM-expressing sex circuitry tuned by fruM function (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the combined experimental data on different manipulation strategies.

claim: fruM expression commences at the wandering third-instar larval stage, peaks at the pupal stage, and thereafter declines but does not disappear after eclosion.
source: Previous findings show that fruM expression commences at the wandering third-instar larval stage, peaks at the pupal stage, and thereafter declines but does not disappear after eclosion (Lee et al., 2000)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Males with fruM knocked down during pupation rarely courted, while males with fruM knocked down during adulthood courted normally toward females.
source: Here we temporally knocked down fruM expression in different developmental stages for 2 days and found that males with fruM knocked down during pupation rarely courted, while males with fruM knocked down during adulthood courted normally toward females.
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data from temporal knockdown experiments.

claim: This is the first direct evidence that fruM is required during development but not adulthood for female-directed courtship behavior.
source: This is the first direct evidence that fruM is required during development but not adulthood for female-directed courtship behavior.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the finding, based on the experimental data.

claim: Knocking down fruM during stages 5 and 6, but not later stages, results in developmental defect in the gustatory receptor neurons innervating VNC.
source: Consistent with these behavioral findings, knocking down fruM during stages 5 and 6, but not later stages, results in developmental defect in the gustatory receptor neurons innervating VNC.
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data on GRN morphology.

claim: Males with fruM knocked down or tra overexpressed during adulthood displayed enhanced male–male courtship or male chaining behaviors.
source: In addition to the role of fruM during development to specify female-directed courtship, we also found a role of fruM during adulthood in suppressing male–male courtship, as males with fruM knocked down or tra overexpressed during adulthood displayed enhanced male–male courtship or male chaining behaviors.
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data from adult-specific manipulation.

claim: Removal of transformer 2 (tra2) specifically during adulthood using a temperature sensitive tra2 allele induced 8 of 96 females to show male-type courtship behaviors.
source: Note that a previous study found that removal of transformer 2 (tra2) specifically during adulthood using a temperature sensitive tra2 allele induced 8 of 96 females to show male-type courtship behaviors (Belote and Baker, 1987)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Expression of FRUM and DSXM during adulthood is sufficient to masculinize CNS to some extent and induce a small fraction of females to display male-like courtship behaviors.
source: which suggests that expression of FRUM and DSXM (by removal of tra2 function in females) during adulthood is sufficient to masculinize CNS to some extent and induce a small fraction of females to display male-like courtship behaviors.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the cited finding about tra2 removal.

claim: fruM expression in the Or47b-expressing olfactory receptor neurons as well as their neuronal sensitivity depend on social experiences during adulthood.
source: Recent studies also found that fruM expression in the Or47b-expressing olfactory receptor neurons as well as their neuronal sensitivity depend on social experiences during adulthood (Hueston et al., 2016; Sethi et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to recent research.

claim: fruM expression during pupation is crucial for neuronal development and reconstruction of adult sex circuitry that allows innate courtship toward females.
source: Based on all these findings, we propose that fruM expression during pupation is crucial for neuronal development and reconstruction of adult sex circuitry that allows innate courtship toward females
evidence: This is a proposed model based on the experimental data and cited research.

claim: fruM expression during adulthood may be activity dependent in at least some neurons and modulates some aspects of courtship (e.g., inhibits male–male courtship).
source: and its expression during adulthood may be activity dependent in at least some neurons and modulates some aspects of courtship (e.g., inhibits male–male courtship).
evidence: This is a proposed model based on the experimental data and cited research.

claim: There are at least two separate mechanisms that fruM contributes to the sex circuitry: one during a critical developmental period to build the female-directed innate courtship into that circuitry, and the other during adulthood to modulate neuronal physiology in an experience-dependent manner.
source: Thus, there are at least two separate mechanisms that fruM contributes to the sex circuitry, one during a critical developmental period to build the female-directed innate courtship into that circuitry, and the other during adulthood to modulate neuronal physiology in an experience-dependent manner.
evidence: This is a proposed model based on the experimental data.

claim: Males with a sex circuitry having wild-type fruM function have innate heterosexual courtship.
source: males with a sex circuitry having wild-type fruM function have innate heterosexual courtship, as they court readily toward females, but do not court males no matter how long they meet
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data on wild-type males.

claim: Males with a sex circuitry having no fruM function lose the innate courtship ability, but have the potential to acquire courtship toward males, females, and even other species in an experience-dependent manner.
source: males with a sex circuitry having no fruM function lose the innate courtship ability, but have the potential to acquire courtship toward males, females, and even other species in an experience-dependent manner
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data on fruM null males.

claim: Males with a sex circuitry having limited fruM expression (e.g., 40%) have innate homosexual courtship.
source: males with a sex circuitry having limited fruM expression (e.g., 40%) have innate homosexual courtship, as they court readily toward other males, but rarely court females
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data on systemic fruM knockdown males.

claim: Males with a sex circuitry having limited fruM expression outside brain (but intact fruM expression in brain) are innately bisexual.
source: males with a sex circuitry having limited fruM expression outside brain (but intact fruM expression in brain) are innately bisexual, as they court equally toward females or males.
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data on outside-brain fruM knockdown males.

claim: Different fruM alleles (e.g., deletions, inversions, or insertions related to fru) showed very different courtship abnormalities.
source: Although previous studies found that different fruM alleles (e.g., deletions, inversions, or insertions related to fru) showed very different courtship abnormalities (Anand et al., 2001; Villella et al., 1997)
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Instead of simply being a master gene that controls all aspects of male courtship, fruM is not absolutely necessary for courtship, but changes the wiring of the sex circuitry during development such that the sex circuitry may function in very different ways.
source: Our study using relatively simple genetic manipulations that generate dramatical different courtship behaviors promoted us to speculate a different view about the role of fruM: instead of simply being a master gene that controls all aspects of male courtship, fruM is not absolutely necessary for courtship, but changes the wiring of the sex circuitry during development such that the sex circuitry may function in very different ways, ranging from innately heterosexual, homosexual, bisexual, to largely experience-dependent acquisition of the behavior.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on the experimental data.

claim: The sex circuitry may function in very different ways, ranging from innately heterosexual, homosexual, bisexual, to largely experience-dependent acquisition of the behavior.
source: fruM is not absolutely necessary for courtship, but changes the wiring of the sex circuitry during development such that the sex circuitry may function in very different ways, ranging from innately heterosexual, homosexual, bisexual, to largely experience-dependent acquisition of the behavior.
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data showing different courtship modes.

claim: Flexibility of the sex circuitry is tuned by different fruM expression, such that changes of fruM regulatory regions during evolution would easily select a suitable functional mode of the sex circuitry.
source: Such flexibility of the sex circuitry is tuned by different fruM expression, such that changes of fruM regulatory regions during evolution would easily select a suitable functional mode of the sex circuitry.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation about evolutionary implications based on the experimental data.

claim: The fruM microRNA specifically knocked down mRNA of fruM, but not the common form of fru.
source: Driving the fruM microRNA by fruGAL4 specifically knocked down mRNA of fruM, but not the common form of fru (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A-C.

claim: fruGAL4 drives expression throughout development and adulthood.

evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D-K.

claim: The anti-FruM antibody successfully labeled male-specific FruM proteins.
source: To validate efficiency of fruM knockdown during specific developmental periods, we generated an antibody against FruM as well as a V5 knock-in into the fru gene (fruV5) to visualize FruM expression. Both tools successfully labeled male-specific FruM proteins (Figure 1—figure supplement 2)
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The anti-FruM antibody also labeled several pairs of false-positive neurons in both wild-type and fruM mutants.

claim: fruM is required for the male-specific midline crossing of GRNs innervating VNC.
source: Thus we set out to examine the morphology of a subset of fruM-positive gustatory receptor neurons (GRNs) innervating the ventral nerve cord (VNC) in tub-GAL80ts/UAS-mCD8GFP; fruGAL4/UAS-fruMi males that have been heat shocked for 2 days in different developmental stages, as it has been found that fruM is required for the male-specific midline crossing of these GRNs (Mellert et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: The GRNs innervating VNC were only labeled in males that have been heat shocked after stage 4, probably because these GRNs were developed after stage 4.
source: We found that these GRNs were only labeled in males that have been heat shocked after stage 4, probably because these GRNs were developed after stage 4 (Figure 1—figure supplement 4A–C), consistent with a previous study (Mellert et al., 2012).
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4A-C and consistent with cited research.

claim: Male–male courtship in fruM knocked down males is higher if tested on food.
source: We found that male–male courtship in fruM knocked down males is higher if tested on food, consistent with a courtship promoting role by food (Grosjean et al., 2011; Pan and Baker, 2014)
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1 and consistent with cited research.

claim: Courtship in wild-type males on food or without food is not changed in the assays.

evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: P1 neurons are important for courtship initiation.

evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.
